rationale: Ono is the customer: it pays the quarterly royalty at 127416-127575 and must let Array and its representatives into its premises to audit the records behind that royalty (114380-115059). business_context: combined franchised-network paper; which state law governs a dispute
rationale: Clause A elects Georgia law without regard to its conflict rules; clause B, spliced in from the second source, elects New York law for the same Agreement. Both are exclusive and neither yields, so the Agreement cannot be governed by both and a party pleading either law breaches the other; the perpetual licence at 39823 is the grant this intake makes. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: IP carve-out deal; which law governs the transferred rights

deadline.deadline_text: Effective as of the applicable Closing Date

rationale: Clause A makes Delaware law govern the IP agreement 'whether arising in contract, tort, equity or otherwise'; clause B, spliced in from the second source, makes California law govern the same Agreement and fixes California law for the merits of any dispute. The two are mutually exclusive and neither contains precedence language, so no course of performance satisfies both; the assignment duty at 38489 is the Seller's. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: franchise and alliance paper; which law applies to the royalty claim

deadline.deadline_text: beginning six (6) months after the Commencement Date

rationale: Clause A says the Agreement will be interpreted and construed exclusively under Texas law, which prevails over any conflict of law; clause B, spliced in from the second source, makes New York law govern the same Agreement without regard to its conflict rules. Both are exclusive and there is no ordering language, so the Agreement cannot be governed by both; the minimum royalty at 22534 is the customer's. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: franchisor review of a grant-back it must be able to keep
rationale: Clause A takes a perpetual, worldwide grant-back of the franchisee's ideas and materials; clause B, spliced in from the second source, lets the service recipient terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with no carve-out preserving licensed rights. The grant is meant to survive the relationship while the termination ends it, so the two cannot both be performed; the grant-back at 66065 is the duty recorded. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: data-migration alliance; can the perpetual licence be ended at will
rationale: Clause A grants a fully paid, perpetual, worldwide licence; clause B, spliced in from the second source, lets the consultant walk away at any time on 120 days' notice. A perpetual grant and an at-will exit are not jointly performable - the exit ends the licence the first clause says runs forever - and neither clause carves the licensed rights out. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document. The perpetual, irrevocable quality is a grant qualifier on this one LIC-GRANT, not a separate obligation (guide Â§3.3, D3), so the excluded `Irrevocable Or Perpetual License` category is used only as the conflict anchor, never as the obligation's category.

business_context: customer exit costing against the supplier remedy waiver
rationale: Clause A requires the customer to pay the Termination Fee as liquidated damages on a partial termination; clause B, spliced in from the second source, says the supplier is not liable and the customer waives all claims for damages of any type whatsoever. The same document therefore requires the payment and extinguishes the claim that supports it; neither clause orders the other. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: termination-fee exposure against the counterparty damages exclusion
rationale: Clause A stipulates that the Termination Fee is payable because the injury from termination cannot be estimated; clause B, spliced in from the second source, states that no party is liable to the other for indirect, special, exemplary, punitive or consequential damages. A stipulated sum for unquantifiable loss is exactly the head clause B excludes, so the fee duty and the exclusion cannot both be performed. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: supply floor against the aggregate liability cap

deadline.deadline_text: forecasted for each Calendar Month of the Firm Zone

rationale: Clause A caps aggregate liability at the product prices paid in the preceding twelve months; clause B, spliced in from the second source, requires the paying party to pay additional sums as damages for non-compliant content with no ceiling. The payment duty reaches beyond the cap by its own terms and neither span yields, so no single course of performance satisfies both. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.

business_context: transition-services review; fees cap against per-day service credits
rationale: Clause A caps a party's liability for services at the fees paid for the specific service that caused the loss; clause B, spliced in from the second source, makes the service provider pay a per-day sum as liquidated damages until conversion is achieved. Once the delay runs long enough the per-day duty exceeds the fee cap, and neither clause carves the other out, so the cap and the accruing payment cannot both hold. Constructed pair: verbatim spans, spliced document.
